name: Education
blurb: Trường lớp, phương pháp học, bằng cấp

words.definitionEn: relating to education, especially at a college or university level
words.example: Students must maintain a high academic standard to qualify for the scholarship.

words.definitionEn: official approval given by an authority, usually to an educational institution or program
words.example: The university lost its accreditation after failing to meet the required standards.

words.definitionEn: graduates or former students of a particular school, college, or university
words.example: Many alumni donate generously to support scholarships for current students.

words.definitionEn: a system of training a new generation of practitioners in a trade or profession with on-the-job training and often some accompanying study
words.example: She decided to pursue an apprenticeship rather than a traditional university degree.

words.definitionEn: the evaluation or estimation of the nature, quality, or ability of someone or something
words.example: Continuous assessment is used to monitor students' progress throughout the semester.

words.definitionEn: an academic degree or qualification, especially the International Baccalaureate or a bachelor's degree
words.example: The International Baccalaureate program is recognized by universities worldwide.

words.definitionEn: a ceremony at which students receive their academic degrees or diplomas
words.example: The commencement speech was delivered by a renowned alumnus.

words.definitionEn: required by law or a rule; obligatory
words.example: In many countries, education is compulsory for children between the ages of 6 and 16.

words.definitionEn: covering a wide range of topics or details; thorough
words.example: A comprehensive curriculum includes both theoretical knowledge and practical skills.

words.definitionEn: a qualification, achievement, or quality that gives someone a basis for trust or authority
words.example: Employers often require candidates to present their academic credentials.

words.definitionEn: the subjects comprising a course of study in a school or college
words.example: The school is revising its curriculum to include more digital literacy.

words.definitionEn: a written overview of a person's education, qualifications, and experience
words.example: Applicants are requested to submit a detailed curriculum vitae with their application.

words.definitionEn: the head of a faculty or department in a college or university
words.example: The dean of the faculty of engineering announced a new research initiative.

words.definitionEn: a qualification awarded by a college or university after completing a course of study
words.example: She earned a degree in economics from a prestigious university.

words.definitionEn: intended to teach, especially in a way that is morally instructive
words.example: The didactic approach of the lecture left little room for student interaction.

words.definitionEn: a certificate awarded by an educational institution for completing a course of study
words.example: He received his diploma at the graduation ceremony.

words.definitionEn: a long essay on a particular subject, especially one written for a university degree
words.example: Her dissertation on climate change policy was highly praised by the committee.

words.definitionEn: a person who leaves school or college before completing a course
words.example: The school implemented programs to reduce the dropout rate among at-risk students.

words.definitionEn: a course or subject that students can choose to study, rather than being compulsory
words.example: Students may take elective courses in fields such as art or music.

words.definitionEn: the process of registering or being registered for a course or program
words.example: Enrollment for the fall semester opens in July.

words.definitionEn: activities that fall outside the regular academic curriculum
words.example: Participating in extracurricular activities can enhance a student's university application.

words.definitionEn: the teaching staff of a university or college, or a department within it
words.example: The faculty of arts and sciences offers a wide range of majors.

words.definitionEn: grade point average; a numerical measure of a student's academic performance
words.example: To maintain his scholarship, he needs to keep his GPA above 3.5.

words.definitionEn: the successful completion of a course of study, especially at a university
words.example: After graduation, she plans to work in the non-profit sector.

words.definitionEn: involving learning through discovery and problem-solving rather than direct instruction
words.example: The heuristic method encourages students to find solutions on their own.

words.definitionEn: considering the whole person or system, rather than just separate parts
words.example: A holistic education aims to develop the intellectual, emotional, and social aspects of a student.

words.definitionEn: involving communication and active participation between the teacher and students
words.example: Interactive learning platforms have become popular in modern classrooms.

words.definitionEn: involving two or more academic disciplines
words.example: The university offers an interdisciplinary program combining business and technology.

words.definitionEn: a period of work experience offered by an organization for a limited period, often to students
words.example: She completed an internship at a marketing firm to gain practical experience.

words.definitionEn: an educational talk given to a group of students, especially at a university
words.example: The professor's lecture on quantum mechanics was both informative and engaging.

words.definitionEn: the ability to read and write
words.example: Improving literacy rates among adults is a key goal of the education program.

words.definitionEn: the formal process of enrolling in a college or university
words.example: Matriculation into the university requires a high school diploma or equivalent.

words.definitionEn: an experienced and trusted advisor who guides a less experienced person
words.example: Each graduate student is assigned a mentor who provides academic guidance.

words.definitionEn: the ability to understand and work with numbers
words.example: Basic numeracy skills are essential for everyday life and many jobs.

words.definitionEn: the method and practice of teaching, especially as an academic subject
words.example: Modern pedagogy emphasizes student-centered learning over traditional lectures.

words.definitionEn: a person of the same age, status, or ability as another, especially in a school context
words.example: Peer assessment can help students develop critical thinking skills.

words.definitionEn: the practice of taking someone else's work or ideas and passing them off as one's own
words.example: Universities have strict policies against plagiarism, and offenders may face expulsion.

words.definitionEn: relating to studies undertaken after completing a first degree
words.example: Many students pursue postgraduate degrees to specialize in their field.

words.definitionEn: designed to improve or correct a student's skills in a particular area
words.example: The school offers remedial classes for students who struggle with mathematics.

words.definitionEn: extremely thorough, exhaustive, or accurate; demanding
words.example: The rigorous academic program prepares students for competitive careers.

words.definitionEn: a financial award given to a student to help pay for education
words.example: She was awarded a full scholarship to study abroad.

words.definitionEn: a small group discussion or class on a particular topic, often at a university
words.example: The seminar on educational technology was attended by 20 graduate students.

words.definitionEn: an outline of the subjects, topics, and readings for a course
words.example: The syllabus for the course includes weekly readings and assignments.

words.definitionEn: a long piece of research-based writing submitted for a higher degree, such as a master's or doctorate
words.example: He defended his thesis on the history of economic thought successfully.

words.definitionEn: an official record of a student's academic performance and courses taken
words.example: Applicants must submit their official transcripts along with the application form.

words.definitionEn: the fee charged for instruction, especially at a college or private school
words.example: Rising tuition costs have made higher education less accessible for many families.

words.definitionEn: a small group session led by a tutor, often used to supplement lectures
words.example: The weekly tutorial gives students the chance to ask questions and discuss ideas.

words.meaningVi: sinh viên đại học chưa tốt nghiệp
words.definitionEn: a student at a college or university who is working towards a first degree
words.example: Undergraduates are required to complete a certain number of credit hours per semester.

words.definitionEn: the student who has the highest academic rank in a graduating class and delivers the farewell speech
words.example: The valedictorian gave an inspiring speech at the graduation ceremony.

words.definitionEn: relating to education that prepares students for a specific trade or career
words.example: Vocational training programs provide practical skills for jobs like plumbing or carpentry.
